scope: Current HSConfig repository implementation on branch codex/hsconfig-contract-spine-guard-wave at commit 17cb4a71511b84c8ca1184936a96db4cbc0bd755, audited after the semantic qualifier fixes. The review covers supported atomic claim kinds, source_contract_matrix policy rows, semantic qualifiers, source claim conflicts, surface gate decisions, builder and router lowering, source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, contract_spine_sentinel, output_ownership_manifest, and reports/operator_summary.json as the only normal apply authority.
verified_strengths: The repository defines exactly 15 supported atomic claim kinds: archetype, mulligan_keep, mulligan_discard, card_role, targeting_rule, combo_sequence, gameplan_posture, hero_power_transform, mechanic_usage, known_bad_pattern, tech_slot, replacement_option, discover_choice, choose_one_choice, and globalvalue_numeric_tuning.

source_contract_matrix requires one policy row for every supported claim kind and fails fast on missing or extra policy or policy-detail rows. Each row exposes a semantic lane, allowed surfaces, required fields, runtime lowerability, a default suppression reason, and operator_gate_impact=diagnostic_only.

The per-surface gate is explicit and narrow. Mulligan accepts only mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard; GlobalValues accepts only gameplan_posture; Combo accepts only combo_sequence; and CardID accepts only the documented CardID behavior claim kinds. globalvalue_numeric_tuning is deliberately suppressed until runtime evidence exists.

The semantic qualifier implementation normalizes timing, zone_scope, target_scope, option_surface, and state_requirements from both nested and convenience fields. It also derives start_of_game and hero_power_transform qualifiers from semantic roles, including static Darkbishop Benedictus claims.

The semantic qualifier fix closes the false-mulligan path: a runtime-lowerable mulligan_keep claim that denotes a non-hand start-of-game effect is rejected with start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand unless its evidence explicitly states opening-hand Mulligan intent.

Semantic qualifiers are intentionally not a new broad lowering authority. The matrix records target_scope for targeting_rule and timing or state requirements for combo_sequence as diagnostic metadata; only the documented claim kind and surface-specific builder prerequisites authorize runtime emission.

source_claim_conflicts now identifies conflicting keep versus discard claims, targeting scopes, combo timings, option choices, and card-role usage versus known bad patterns. Its resolution is explicitly report-visible rather than silent.

The package builder wires the source bundle into claim_conflict_report.json, source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, output_ownership_manifest.json, and the operator summary. This provides a trace from normalized evidence through generated runtime files without making diagnostics a second writer.

source_contract_audit records per-claim lifecycle information across policy, surface gate, builder or router, emitted or suppressed runtime effect, first missing link, and operator impact. source_to_runtime_explainability projects that audit into claim and card rows with missing runtime files and next-source actions.

contract_spine_sentinel is read-only and clean at the audited commit. It found no policy or spine claim-kind drift, no apply-authority fields in diagnostic rows, no diagnostic report tokens in active apply paths, no unclassified expected outputs, no forbidden legacy runtime surfaces, and a legacy_no_op source-informed flag.

output_ownership_manifest classifies report outputs, runtime surfaces, diagnostics, unknown outputs, and forbidden legacy surfaces. reports/operator_summary.json is the single manifest gate row; Presume.json and Concede.json are classified as forbidden normal-path legacy surfaces.

The normal apply path is re-checked in code. evaluate_apply_gate reads reports/operator_summary.json, verifies required runtime files and the generated-file inventory against disk, and runtime_apply rejects a forged, missing, or mismatched gate before runtime mutation.

The focused contract, qualifier, conflict, ownership, explainability, sentinel, and apply-authority suite passed at the audited commit: 133 passed in 4.87 seconds. The live contract-spine sentinel command also returned status=clean and apply_blocking=false.
correctness_gaps: Claim-conflict detection is diagnostic only and is not consumed by the shared surface gates or builder/router lowering functions. The report identifies contradictory lowerable claims but does not implement a centralized precedence or suppression rule before runtime rows are built; a future end-to-end regression test should prove the emitted behavior for each conflict family.

Semantic qualifier merge precedence is intentionally simple: recognized nested qualifier values are loaded first and matching top-level convenience fields overwrite them. The normalizer does not preserve both source values or emit a qualifier-conflict diagnostic when those two representations disagree, so upstream source normalization can discard contradictory qualifier evidence.

CardID conditional claims remain dependent on documented runtime block and identity detail. card_role, mechanic_usage, known_bad_pattern, discover_choice, and choose_one_choice can stay suppressed even when the source claim is semantically valid, leaving a technically load-safe package with thinner behavior coverage.

combo_sequence remains runtime-lowerable in policy but requires complete builder inputs. Incomplete sequences are suppressed, so a source may be correctly classified while still producing no Combo.json row.

The contract-spine sentinel detects diagnostic token consumption only in its enumerated ACTIVE_APPLY_PATHS. A future runtime-writing module must be added to that list or equivalent coverage, otherwise the static scan can miss a new apply route that consumes a diagnostic artifact.

The policy matrix and source-document model are kept in sync by current tests, but a future claim-kind addition still requires coordinated updates across the supported set, policy matrix, surface gate, conformance spine, builder/router ownership, documentation, and tests. Omitting one layer can cause unsupported or unmapped behavior rather than a useful runtime row.
slimness_gaps: The repository now produces several related diagnostic artifacts: claim conflicts, source contract audit, source-to-runtime explainability, source claim gaps, conformance, ownership, and operator-summary projections. They remain acceptably separated today, but duplicating routing or gate logic among them would create a difficult-to-maintain second contract system.

semantic_qualifiers adds a compact common vocabulary, but each additional qualifier alias, claim-kind-specific interpretation, or builder special case increases the synchronization burden across normalization, verification, policy metadata, and tests.

output_ownership_manifest is intentionally descriptive. Turning its classifications or counts into another operational permission surface would duplicate the operator summary gate and make normal operation harder to reason about.

Reintroducing Presume.json or Concede.json into the normal output path would widen runtime validation, ownership classification, documentation, and drift checks without improving the minimal load-safe package contract.
autonomy_gaps: Exact option identity is still required for Discover and Choose One lowering. Broad guide prose remains visible and diagnostic but cannot autonomously create a CardID option row.
Combo lowering requires structured sequence details; source collection that only identifies cards or broad combo intent cannot autonomously produce a complete Combo.json action sequence.

Numeric GlobalValues tuning remains outside Step 1 autonomy because globalvalue_numeric_tuning requires runtime evidence. This is an intentional boundary, but it means static source research cannot change numeric tuning values.

Conflict reports can prevent an honest source-backed-strong assessment but do not block a technically valid normal load-safe apply. This preserves any-deck autonomy, while placing the responsibility for evidence repair in diagnostics rather than requiring manual approval.

The legacy allow_source_informed parameter is a no-op, so no caller can obtain a weaker alternate apply permission. That removes a bypass path but also intentionally prevents source-depth warnings from being overridden through a flag.
guardrails_to_keep: Keep claim_kind, claim readiness, trust ceiling, and the per-surface gate as the only source-to-runtime routing authority; do not infer runtime rows from free-text importance or generic gameplan prose.
Keep the start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand rejection and the requirement for explicit opening-hand language before a start-of-game effect can enter Mulligan.json.
Keep semantic qualifiers normalized at source ingress and static claim generation, but keep targeting and combo qualifiers diagnostic unless a documented builder contract explicitly consumes them.
Keep source_claim_conflicts report-visible and make any future automated resolution explicit, source-preserving, and covered by end-to-end builder tests rather than silently selecting a winner.

Keep source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, source contract conformance, output ownership, and contract-spine sentinel diagnostic-only. None should grant or deny normal runtime apply permission.
Keep reports/operator_summary.json as the sole normal apply authority, with evaluate_apply_gate and runtime_apply re-evaluating it against the actual package before a write.
Keep allow_source_informed as a backward-compatible no-op instead of adding a second apply path.
Keep the strict output ownership rules: exactly one gate report, no unclassified expected outputs, and no normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json surfaces.
Keep source-depth, semantic, conflict, and mechanic warnings visible without converting them into hard runtime blocks for an otherwise valid load-safe package.
recommended_next_design: Keep the present contract spine and single-gate architecture. The next focused improvement should be an end-to-end conflict-lowering policy: either suppress mutually contradictory claims before builders run or make a documented deterministic precedence decision with preserved evidence and regression coverage. Do not make semantic qualifiers, conflict reports, explainability reports, ownership manifests, or sentinel results into additional apply gates.
